steps.body: On a number line, equivalent fractions land on the very same POINT. 1/2 and 2/4 and 4/8 are one location wearing three names.
steps.narration: On a number line, equivalent fractions land on the very same POINT. 1/2 and 2/4 and 4/8 are one location wearing three names.

widget.prompt: On a FOURTHS line, place the mark that also names 1/2.

commonPlacements.feedback: 1/4 is one jump — half as far as the halfway point.
4/4 is the whole trip, landing on 1.

widget.successFeedback: 2/4 — two of four jumps, the same point 1/2 occupies.
widget.lowFeedback: Jumps run FORWARD from 0, so a landing behind the target is short of it — count the jumps again.
widget.highFeedback: That is beyond the halfway point — two of the four jumps is where 1/2 sits.

predict.reveal: Two of four jumps covers the same distance as one of two — one point, two names.

cml.actionGoal: Cut, count, and compare equal pieces to see what g3f line equiv really names.
invariants: A fraction names equal shares of ONE whole: the denominator says how many equal pieces the whole became, and the numerator counts them, which is what makes g3f line equiv comparable at all.
misconceptions: Calling unequal pieces fractions, reading the denominator as a count, or comparing fractions that came from different-sized wholes.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: If the whole changed size, which of these comparisons would stop being trustworthy?

commonErrors.feedback: The bottom was multiplied by 4, so the top must be too — otherwise the value changes.
Renaming SCALES both numbers; adding 4 to the top breaks the ratio.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Name the equal pieces the whole was cut into, then count how many of them the question is about.

steps.body: That shared point is the proof: if two fractions land together, they are equal, no matter how different the numbers look.

widget.prompt: On a ruler marked in eighths, which mark lands exactly on 1/2?

options.label: The 4/8 mark
options.feedback: Correct — four of the eight equal jumps is half the trip, so 4/8 and 1/2 name the same point.

options.label: The 2/8 mark
options.feedback: 2/8 is only a quarter of the way — two jumps out of eight, not four.

options.label: The 1/8 mark
options.feedback: 1/8 is a single jump from zero, nowhere near the halfway point of eight jumps.

options.label: There is no such mark
options.feedback: Eighths do land on a half: because 8 is even, the midpoint falls exactly on a mark.
